english: Two houses stood by the river. Good-Fame lived in one house, Man-Mind lived in the other. Good-Fame stole Man-Mind's horse and killed him. Man-Mind's orphan grew up and killed Good-Fame with a heavy [blow/stone]. Now Good-Fame's kin killed him in the row/path. The grandsons fought in the field and fell. No one gave the blood-price and no one accepted it. The women became widows and lamented. Now grass grows over their hearths.

Kin of the slayer and kin of the dead, (you two) hear. I call the two houses. The slayer struck him with a spear. Now I decide: let him give a hundred cows and ten horses. Let the dead man's orphans take them and let blood not be poured. Let them swear this by Perkwunos. Whoever breaks this agreement, may the gods punish him.

True-Fame, an old man's son, insulted/harmed a guest at a feast. The guest's kin came to the settlement and demanded payment. The elder spoke to True-Fame: 'Pay the guest the blood-price.' True-Fame said: 'I will not pay.' Then the elder decided: 'Leave our home. You are not my son.' The youth left, and the old man gave the payment with his own cattle. There was peace between the two houses. The old man's tears poured at the door.

Elder, hear me. Good-Horse killed my brother at the feast. That I declare. Do you want blood or the blood-price? I want blood. My brother was very dear to me. If you pour his blood, his brothers will harm you. Take the wealth and let your children live. I take the wealth. I do not forget my brother.

Who, elder, lived in the empty house? My grandfather lived here. His enemies burned the house with fire. Why did they burn it? He had killed their father. Now their young men killed my grandfather, and I [?] them. Where are your grandsons? The grandsons are now no more. The blood-price/feud swallowed them. Alone I sit by the door.

Whoever kills a free man, let him give the dead man's kin a hundred cows. Whoever kills a woman, let him also give a hundred cows. Whoever strikes a child, let him pay twice. If he does not give, let the kin of the dead take his blood. If they accept the blood-price, let no one pour blood.
